catalog: executed and proposed witness inventory (research stage)
labels: executed_by_candidate = run via admitted isolated python_execute; receipts include code/data sha256, stdout sha256, exit code. These are isolated component checks and do not establish full application behavior. proposed = UNEXECUTED.

executed.claim: Stored annotation coordinates must be float64: float32 collapses large-field coordinates and merges nearby vertices; float64 survives JSON round-trip exactly.
executed.expected_justification: IEEE-754 binary32 has a 24-bit significand, so near 6.0e4 the representable spacing is about 0.0039; a coordinate 60000.001 cannot be represented exactly; two vertices 0.0003 px apart fall within one float32 spacing. Python float is binary64 and json.dumps/loads round-trips binary64 exactly via repr.
executed.stdout:
x_true        = 60000.001
x_float32     = 60000.0
error_px      = -0.000999999996565748 ( 0.000999999996565748 px )
float32 ULP@6e4= 0.0
v1_f32 != v2_f32 : False -> vertices 0.0003 px apart collide in float32: True
json roundtrip exact: True 60000.00123456789
executed.honest_notes: The 'ULP' probe line printed 0.0 because adding 2**-9 to 60000.0 round-trips to the same float32 under struct pack/unpack - a degenerate probe that itself illustrates float32 granularity at that magnitude; the error and vertex-collision lines carry the finding.
executed.scope_limits: Pure arithmetic on number encodings; says nothing about any viewer, storage engine, or application.

executed.claim: Scale/translation application order is semantically load-bearing: identical numbers yield physical positions 10 px apart under the two orders, and inverting with the wrong order recovers the wrong pixel index. Fixes the project convention to NGFF 0.4's 'scale then translation'.
executed.expected_justification: s*i+t (scale then translate) and s*(i+t) (translate then scale) are different affine maps for s!=1 and t!=0; with s=0.5, t=10, i=2 they give 11.0 and 6.0 um; inverse of 11.0 under the wrong order is 11/0.5-10=12 instead of 2. Consistent with NGFF 0.4 §3.3/§3.4 (S1).
executed.stdout:
index i = 2.0 px ; scale s = 0.5 um/px ; translation t = 10.0 um
apply scale then translation  : 11.0 um
apply translation then scale  : 6.0 um
differ: True ; delta = 5.0 um = 10.0 px
recover index from p=11: (p-t)/s = 2.0  ; wrong-order inverse p/s-t = 12.0
executed.scope_limits: Algebraic check only; corroborates the convention choice sourced to S1; does not test any implementation of the transform service.
